source.title: The New Contenders
source.summary: De-dollarization, BRICS, CBDCs, crypto. Rhetoric vs reality in the challenge to dollar dominance.
source.author: Islamic Economics
source.body_text: Everyone talks about de-dollarization, but the dollar's structural advantages are enormous and no alternative comes close. BRICS ambitions face coordination problems. China's yuan internationalization requires capital account openness that Beijing resists. Central Bank Digital Currencies offer financial inclusion but raise surveillance concerns. The Bitcoin and crypto Islamic debate continues. This episode separates signal from noise: the trend at the margins is real, but the dollar system isn't going anywhere soon. Muslim-majority economies remain largely passive observers rather than shapers of whatever comes next.

x.single_post: De-dollarization is mostly noise. The dollar has structural advantages so vast that BRICS struggles with basic coordination problems while China won't open its capital account.
thread: De-dollarization is mostly noise. The dollar has structural advantages so vast that BRICS struggles with basic coordination problems while China won't open its capital account.
Everyone talks about alternatives but yuan internationalization requires Beijing to give up capital controls. They won't do it.
CBDCs offer financial inclusion but come with surveillance concerns that make Bitcoin debates look simple.
The trend at the margins is real but the system isn't changing. Muslim economies remain observers, not shapers. https://islamiceconomics.github.io/podcast.html#ep-mm-5

linkedin.post: The de-dollarization narrative dominates financial discussions, but separating rhetoric from reality reveals a different picture. The dollar's structural advantages remain enormous. BRICS nations struggle with basic coordination while China won't open capital accounts for yuan internationalization. CBDCs offer financial inclusion possibilities but introduce surveillance concerns that complicate Islamic finance debates. The trend at the margins is real, but the core monetary system shows remarkable resilience. For Muslim-majority economies, this creates a strategic challenge: remaining passive observers rather than active shapers of the global financial architecture. Listen to the full analysis: https://islamiceconomics.github.io/podcast.html#ep-mm-5

The trend at the margins is real, but the core system shows remarkable resilience.
